purpose: Prose -> Danbooru-tag mappings for anime SDXL checkpoints. Kept as data, not just prose in SKILL.md, so it can be extended programmatically without re-reading the whole skill.

provenance.how_entries_are_earned: An entry belongs here only after the prose form was observed to silently DROP the trait on a real generation. Guessed synonyms are noise -- they make the table look authoritative without being tested.

tag_order_note: Earlier tags carry more weight. Always lead with the count tag; these models are heavily conditioned on it. Include 'solo' or extra characters drift in.

resolved_failures.original_claim: 'white labcoat with purple stars' failed because SDXL cannot bind an attribute to one noun when two garments compete.
resolved_failures.why_it_was_wrong: The reference art (aria-assistant/assistant/web/aria.jpg) was not consulted before diagnosing. Aria's purple stars are FLOATING DECORATION around her, not a print on the coat. The model was refusing to render a garment pattern that does not exist in the design. Attribute binding was never tested, because the request itself was malformed.
resolved_failures.lesson: Look at the reference before explaining why the model 'failed'. A confident architectural explanation for a prompt that described the wrong thing is worse than no explanation -- it closes the question and sends the next attempt toward regional prompting or LoRA training for no reason.

known_failures.symptom: Floating decorative elements and a flat white background are mutually exclusive in one prompt.
known_failures.observed: animagine-xl-4.0, seed 4242, 2026-08-17. With 'purple star, star (symbol), floating stars, sparkle' the stars render correctly but the background becomes a dramatic blue/purple starfield, overriding 'white background, simple background'. Negating the atmosphere ('starry background, night sky, sparkle, glowing') restores the flat white background but removes the floating stars along with it.
known_failures.cause: Booru training couples floating-decoration tags to the dramatic compositions they appear in. The decoration and the background treatment are one learned concept, not two independent ones.
untested_options: Character LoRA trained on a set that deliberately VARIES the background, so the model learns 'Aria has floating stars' separately from any one background
Generate on the starfield, then composite/inpaint the background to white
known_failures.status: NO TESTED FIX. The LoRA option is the reason a training set must vary its backgrounds rather than standardising on white.
